notes.claim: The two sides of an equation are equal, but in an inequality one side may be greater or less than the other.
Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a positive number keeps the sign, and by a negative number reverses it.
On a number line, the circle at the end of an inequality's answer is unshaded (open) for < and > and shaded (filled) for ≤ and ≥.
A minus sign in an inequality does not by itself mean the sign reverses: reverse it only when multiplying or dividing each side by a negative number.

sources.title: 2.5 Solve Linear Inequalities - Intermediate Algebra 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: When we divide or multiply an inequality by a positive number, the inequality sign stays the same. When we divide or multiply an inequality by a negative number, the inequality sign reverses.

sources.title: Inequalities - KS3 Maths - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The two sides in an equation are equal. This is not the case in an inequality, as one side may be greater than (or less than) the other.

sources.title: Inequalities - KS3 Maths - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The circle is unshaded for < and > The circle is shaded for ≤ and ≥

sources.title: Solving Inequalities 2.6b
sources.quote: A negative sign in an inequality does not necessarily mean you must reverse the inequality symbol. Only reverse the inequality symbol when you multiply or divide each side by a negative number.
